title: Owen's Defense (e6 b6)
description: A setup which is possible against EVERY White opening. Quite tricky and often results in winning a central pawn early.

r2qk2r/1b1p1ppp/1pn1pn2/8/1b2P3/2NB4/PPP.text: And when White castles, we will capture on c3, shattering their queenside pawns.

r2qk2r/pb1p1ppp/1Pn1pn2/8/1b2P3/2NB4/PPP.text: If they take another pawn, we can simply recapture and open up our rook.

r3k2r/1bqp1ppp/1pn1pn2/8/4P3/2PB4/P1PN1P.text: We develop our queen. We have open lines, and the isolated pawns on the a and c-files will come under pressure!

rn1qk1nr/pbp2ppp/1p1pp3/4P3/1b1P4/2N2N2/.text: This move allows us to strike immediately at the center with 5...d6, and we will have easy development of our knights along our second rank.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/3P4/1b2P3/2N2N2/.text: White can try pushing the other central pawn. This will turn out to be premature, as we can bring further pressure to bear on the center by developing our king's knight.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/4P3/1b1P4/2N2N2/.text: White can opt to gain space.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1b1PP3/2NB1N2/.text:
This option, defending the pawn, will also be seen later on. But in here we can demonstrate motifs using a lesser-known line White might play.

We will reply by developing our knight, putting further pressure on the center.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1b1PP3/2NQ1N2/.text: White defends e4 with the queen. We will develop our king's knight on e7, where it is safe from an e5 pawn thrust, and where it also supports a ...d5 pawn push.

rn1qk2r/pb1p1ppp/1p2pn2/2P5/1b2P3/2NB4/P.text: Naturally, White can simply take. We will reply, not by recapturing, but with further development. Bringing our knight to c6 will also discourage e5 by White.

rn1qk2r/pb1p1ppp/1p2pn2/2p5/1b1PP3/P1NB4.text:
White could also attack our bishop, after all our c5 pawn push has taken away any retreat squares.

We will capture on d4, with a counterattack on the c3-knight.

rn1qk2r/pb1p1ppp/1p2pn2/8/1P1pP3/2NB4/1P.text: White takes our bishop, so we will capture their knight.

rn1qk2r/pb1p1ppp/1p2pn2/8/1P2P3/2PB4/2PN.text: White recaptures the pawn on c3. The exchanges have resulted in material parity.

rn1qk2r/pbp1nppp/1p2p3/3p4/1b1PP3/2NQ1N2.text: We can strike in the center! In the following studies, we'll analyze a bit deeper into the middle game!

rn1qk2r/pbpp1ppp/1p2pn2/3P2B1/1b2P3/2N2N.text: White pins our knight, trying to neutralize our pressure. We will reply by pushing the h-pawn, and putting a question to the bishop.

rn1qk2r/pbpp1ppp/1p2pn2/8/1b1PP3/2NB4/PP.text:
One option is for White to retreat, defending e4 and breaking the pin. The knight on f3 supported the d-pawn, but none of our pieces are currently attacking d4.

Therefore, we will target the d4-pawn right away.

rn1qk2r/pbppnppp/1p2p3/8/1b1PP3/2NQ1N2/P.text: White develops their bishop and gets ready to castle.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/2N2N2/PPP.text:
White develops to c3, supporting their center! The two knights setup is complete!

We will respond by developing our dark-squared bishop, pinning the c3-knight. This will leave White with four options which we will examine in this study.

rn2k2r/pbpp1pp1/1p2pq1p/3P4/1b2P3/2N2N2/.text: But when we recapture, White is in trouble because of the lack of support for their overextended central pawns and our pressure on c3.

rn2k2r/pbqp1ppp/1p2pn2/8/1P2P3/2PB4/2PN1.text: Our queen comes out to c7, putting pressure on c3.

rnbqkbnr/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/5N2/PPP2P.text: White develops, supporting the center. We will counter by putting pressure on the e4-pawn.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/4p3/8/3PP3/8/PPP2PPP/R.text:
A second pawn joins the center for White, and the bishop's diagonal is opened.

We will reply with 2...b6, fianchettoing our bishop, as will be our intention throughout this course.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
Welcome to the first study of this course! 

In this study we will demonstrate our e6/b6/Bb7 setup, and we'll see what to do after White plays both their pawns to e4/d4 and their knights to c3 and f3.

Against 1.e4, we play 1...e6.

r2qk2r/p1ppnppp/1p2p3/4P3/3P4/2QB1P2/PPP.text:
We'll bring our knight to e7 where it will help cover the d5 and f5 squares. 

If a rook comes to the g-file once we have castled kingside, g6 will be a good move to stop counterplay on the file.

We may consider bringing a rook to the c-file in combination with a ...c5 pawn break in order to open up a line against the white king.

rn1q1rk1/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/4P3/3P4/2PB1P2/P.text:
The king gets to safety. 

We should expect some sort of kingside attack from White, but the relative lack of minor pieces means White has fewer forces to attack us with.

We can push ...f5 to block White's bishop, and potentially also g6 to blunt pressure on the g-file.

If they decide to take it en passant, our queen will get nicely activated along the f-file and exert some pressure.

rn1q1rk1/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/4P3/3Pb3/2P2N2/P.text:
We castle into to safety.

Our e4-bishop is a strong piece, giving us good control over the light squares and long diagonal.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1b1PP3/2NB1N2/.text: This moves adds another defender to e4, as the knight on c3 is pinned. We will add another piece placing pressure on e4.

rn1qk2r/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/4P3/1b1P4/2NB1P2/.text: Recapturing the bishop. We will continue to exchange minor pieces. Another decent option would be to finish our development with 9...Nc6.

rn1qk2r/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/4P3/1b1Pb3/2N2N2/.text:
White castles, and we need to be careful! The White knight is now unpinned, and it can take our bishop on e4 if we allow it.

Therefore we will remove the danger by capturing on c3, damaging White's pawn structure.

rn1qk2r/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/4P3/3P4/2PB1P2/P1.text:
White can recapture and get another pawn to support the center. 

A player might choose this option if they want more open lines.

rn1qk2r/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/4P3/3P4/2QB1P2/PP.text: Other players might choose to recapture with the queen. We will reply by developing our knight.

rn1qk2r/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/4P3/3Pb3/2P2N2/P1.text: White recaptures the only way possible.

rn1qk2r/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/4P3/1b1P4/2NB1N2/.text:
White recaptures with the queen and develops her at the same time.

We will take on f3, doubling White's kingside pawns and also removing a defender of the d4-pawn.

rn1qk2r/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/4P3/1b1PB3/2N2N2/.text: White might opt to relieve some of the pressure by capturing our knight. We will continue normally by recapturing.

rn1qk2r/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/4P3/1b1Pn3/2NB1N2.text: This move breaks the pin and thus attacks our e4-knight! We will reply by capturing on d2, gaining the bishop pair.

rn1qk2r/pbpp1ppp/1p2pn2/4P3/1b1P4/2NB1N2.text: The e-pawn attacks the knight, and removes itself from danger. We will utilize the pin on the c3-knight to bring our knight to an aggressive post on e4.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/2N2N2/PPP.text: White develops with Nc3, defending e4. We will respond with ...Bb4, pinning the knight.

rnbqkbnr/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/5N2/PPP2P.text: The knight develops, defending d4. We play our traditional fianchetto.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/4p3/8/3PP3/8/PPP2PPP/R.text: White places a second pawn in the center, and we will reply with 2...b6 to fianchetto our bishop.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
This second study will look at what happens after 5.Bd3 to defend the e4 pawn. In particular, we will look at the continuation 5...Nf6, adding another attacker, and in response the pawn advance 6.e5.

White starts by establishing a central presence with e4. As before, we will reply with ...e6.

2kr3r/1bpqbp2/ppn1p1pp/3pP3/B2P2Q1/2P1B3.text: White finally develops their queen's bishop.

2kr3r/pbpq1ppp/1pn1p3/3pP3/3P4/B1PB1N1P/.text:
We managed to get our king to safety and castle. It's clear that White has no compensation for the exchange. 

We have solid pawn cover and there is no meaningful attack on the king to show for the sacrificed material.

2krq2r/1bp1bp2/ppn1p1pp/3pP3/B2P2Q1/2P1B.text: We continue to disentangle from the pin, with the idea of the queen heading to the kingside to assist with impending pawn pushes against the opposing king.

2r1k2r/1bpn1ppp/1p2pn2/p6q/P1PP1B2/3B1N2.text: White redeploys the rook to an active post. We will simply castle, getting our king into safety.

2r1k2r/pbpn1ppp/1p2pn2/7q/P1PP1B2/3B1N2/.text:
Gaining queenside space, and with the idea of activating the a1-rook by opening the a-file. Launching an attack.

We will prevent this by pushing ...a5 ourselves.

2r2rk1/1bpn1ppp/1p2pn2/pR5q/P1PP1B2/3B1N.text: Attacking our queen. We will block with c5, simultaneously targeting the white center.

5rk1/1b1n1ppp/1p2pn2/pRr4q/P1P2B2/3B1N2/.text: And we recapture with our rook to avoid pinning our knight. White has the bishop pair, but our pawn structure is far better.

r2q1k1r/pb2b1pp/1p2Q3/2ppR3/8/3B4/PBP2PP.text: White keeps the attack going. Now Rf5+ is a big threat. We will preempt it by blocking the file with our bishop.

r2q1k1r/pb4pp/1p2Qb2/2p2R2/3p4/3B4/PBP2P.text: We could also have played ...Qe7. It is coming next move and we are safe, with an extra rook.

r2q1k1r/pb4pp/1p2Qb2/2pp1R2/8/3B4/PBP2PP.text: Rf5 pins our bishop to the king, and threatens to invade with Bxf6. We can still use our pawns to block the bishop.

r2qk2r/pb2b1pp/1p2Q3/2pp4/8/3B4/PBP2PPP/.text:
White redeploys the bishop on another diagonal, attacking the g7-pawn. 

We will defend it with our king, and this also breaks the pin on the e7-bishop.

r2qk2r/pb3ppp/1pp1p3/1B1pP3/1n1P4/2b1BN2.text: We block the check, and pose a question to the bishop.

r2qk2r/pbp1b1pp/1p2Q3/3p4/8/B2B4/P1P2PPP.text: White adds another attacker! We will block the attacking bishop with our c-pawn.

r2qk2r/pbp1bp2/1pn1p1pp/1B1pP3/3P2Q1/2P2.text: White creates a strong central pawn chain. We will move our queen, preparing the king's escape to the queenside.

r2qk2r/pbp1bpp1/1pn1p2p/1B1pP3/3P2Q1/5N2.text: The queen attacks the g7-pawn. If we were to castle, we would suddenly find ourselves walking into trouble after Bxh6, when the g-pawn is pinned. Therefore we push the g-pawn forward to g6.

r2qk2r/pbp2pp1/1pn1p2p/1B1pP3/1b1P1Q2/5N.text: This move pins our knight which was defending our bishop! We can't leave it hanging, so we will retreat it to e7.

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2Rb2/3p4/6Q1/B2B4/P1P2P.text: A rook sacrifice! White plays with the idea of catching the king in the center. We have no choice but to accept.

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/1B1pP3/1n1P4/2b1BN2.text: White could check on b5, but this is met with a pawn interposition.

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/1n1P4/1RbBBN2/.text: White can attack our bishop, which has no escape squares, but we will capture on d3 in reply.

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/1n1P4/2R1BN2/P.text: We retreat the knight. White can try to trick us with 14.Qb5+, forking the king and knight, but we would have  14...Nc6 15.Rxc6 Qd7 and we escape by the skin of our teeth!

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/3N4/B1bB4/P1P1.text: White exchanges the knight, and we recapture.

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/3P4/1RbQBN2/P1.text: Recapturing with the queen, but our bishop can now sneak out to a5!

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/3P4/2RnBN2/P1P.text: If rook takes on d3 instead of the queen recapture, then our knight can escape via b4.

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/3b2Q1/B2B4/P1P.text: This move forks our bishop and g7 pawn. The only reasonable solution is to grab the pawn on e5!

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pb3/6Q1/B2B4/P1P2P.text: White attacks our bishop with the rook, going for activity on the open lines. We will retreat the bishop, maintaining the connection to g7.

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/b2pP3/3P4/1R1QBN2/P.text: We have managed to retain our extra pawn, and we have the bishop pair.

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1pn1p3/3pP3/1b1P1Q2/3B1N2.text:
The queen gives the dark-squared bishop a square on e3. Additionally, she stares down at f7. 

We need to treat the active white pieces with respect, and accordingly, we play ...h6, denying the knight access to g5.

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1pn1p3/3pP3/3P4/2bBBN2/P1.text: Alternatively, White can defend d4 with the bishop. We will reply by harassing the strong d3-bishop with our knight.

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1pn1p3/3pP3/3P4/2bBQN2/P1.text: White defends d4. We will use the freshly developed knight on c6 to support the escape of our bishop via b4.

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1pn1p3/3pP3/3P4/B1bB1N2/P.text: White sacrifices the d4-pawn with the idea that taking away our kingside castling rights is sufficient compensation. Spoiler alert: it isn't.

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1pn1p3/3pP3/3P4/B2B1N1P/P.text: This move gives the king some breathing room. Our plan proceeds uninterrupted.

r2qk2r/pbp3pp/1p2Qb2/3p4/8/B2B4/P1P2PPP/.text: White recaptures with check! Our king has no squares, but we can block with the bishop.

r3k2r/1bpqbp2/ppn1p1pp/3pP3/B2P2Q1/2P5/P.text: White chooses to maintain the pin, but we now have the potential option of ...b5. In the meantime, we will get the king into relative safety on the queenside.

r3k2r/pbpn1ppp/1p2pn2/3q4/2PP4/3B1N2/P1P.text: This is a common advance by White, expanding in the center. We will keep the queen actively placed by moving it to h5.

r3k2r/pbpn1ppp/1p2pn2/7q/2PP1B2/3B1N2/P1.text: Developing a piece and attacking c7. We will defend c7 with our rook, and prepare a future pawn push with ...c5.

r3k2r/pbpq1ppp/1pn1p3/3pP1B1/3P4/2bB1N2/.text: We're a pawn up and we have pressure on d4. We will still have to be careful on the kingside. A future ...h6 may be a useful prophylactic move.

r3k2r/pbpqbp2/1pn1p1pp/1B1pP3/3P2Q1/2P5/.text: White prepares to expand with f4, and a later f5. We will continue by taking steps to break the awkward pin on the a4-e8 diagonal.

rn1q1rk1/pb3ppp/1p2p3/2ppP3/1b1P2Q1/2NB4.text: We can castle safely here as there is no danger of a Bxh7 sacrifice.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1b1PP3/2NB1N2/.text: White defends e4. We will develop our knight, adding another attacker on e4.

rn1qk2r/p1p2ppp/1p2pB2/8/1b1Pb3/2N2N2/PP.text: As White would lose after 9.Qxe4 Nxe4 10.Bxd8 Nxc3, removing the knight defending our bishop on e4 is the best option for our opponent.

rn1qk2r/pb2bppp/1p2p3/2ppP3/3P4/2NB1N2/P.text: We will strike at the base of the central pawn chain, and we are happy to have the bishop pair.

rn1qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP1B1/3P4/2bB1N2/.text:
White can try an In-between move! The rook remains en prise, but our queen, which is more valuable, is under attack.

We will sidestep the threat from the bishop.

rn1qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/1b1P4/2NB1N2/.text:
White recaptures. We will redeploy the bishop. 

The pin wasn't so useful anymore as the pressure on e4 has been resolved, and now Black guards the g5 square with bishop and queen to make castling safer.

rn1qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/1b1P4/2NB4/PP.text:
Taking with the knight is also an option.

We will strike at the center with greater potency now that the knight no longer defends the d4-pawn.

rn1qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/1b1P4/2PB1N2/.text: White recaptures, as they should. We will win a pawn with our bishop, and attack the a1-rook.

rn1qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/1b1PB3/2N2N2/.text:
This looks natural and resolves the tension on c3, but it isn't particularly good.

We will take on e4.

rn1qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/1b1Pn3/2NB1N2.text: White gets the king to safety. Additionally, they unpin the c3 knight! We will take on c3, and win a pawn.
White breaks the pin with this move: now three pieces attack the e4-knight. We will solve the problem by capturing on d2.

rn1qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/3P4/2bB1N2/P1.text: White's rook gets out of danger. Our bishop is a little short of safe squares. In the meantime, we will continue by developing our knight and putting pressure on d4.

rn1qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/3P4/B1bB1N2/P.text: White can choose to play in a sacrificial style. We will show no fear, and accept it!

rn1qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/3P4/B2B1N2/P1.text: White recaptures, and we develop the knight, getting ready to go Qd7 and 0-0-0.

rn1qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/4P1N1/1b1Pp3/2N5/P.text: The knight goes to g5 but now it is no longer defending the d4-pawn.

rn1qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2pn2/3P4/1b1P4/2NB1N2/.text:
A natural response. White gets rid of the pressure by trading off a pair of pawns.

We will capture on d5 with the queen, exploiting the pin on the c3-knight in order to bring our queen to an active location.

rn1qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2pn2/3p2B1/1b1PP3/2NB1.text:
This is another way to deal with the pressure on e4. White pins our knight to the queen, reducing its central influence.

We will capture on e4 and get a good position.

rn1qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2pn2/3pP3/1b1P4/2NB1N2.text:
This is a very natural response. White thinks: if the pressure is too much on e4 to handle, just push the pawn to e5! There's less pressure there.

We will respond by bringing our attacked knight into the outpost on e4.

rn1qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p2pn2/6B1/1b1PB3/2N2N2/.text: This is the only reasonable recapture. We will continue by taking on e4 with our bishop.

rn1qk2r/pbpp1ppp/1p2pn2/8/1b1PP3/2NB1N2/.text: Qe2 adds another defender for White, and we will continue to add pressure, while establishing one of our pawns in the center!

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/2N2N2/PPP.text: White defends e4. We will pin the knight, thus placing e4 under attack once more.

rn2k2r/p1p2ppp/1p2pB2/3q4/1b1Pb3/2N2N2/P.text:
We defend our strong bishop! White's knight on c3 isn't attacking us since it is pinned by the bishop on b4, and White will have to waste time saving the f6-bishop.

Note that 10.Bxg7 Rg8 doesn't help White, as the g2-pawn will fall.

rn2k2r/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/4P1N1/1b1qp3/2N5/PP.text: We are now a healthy pawn up, and we are attacking both c3 and e5.

rn2k2r/pbp2ppp/1p2pn2/3q4/1b1P4/2NB1N2/P.text: This is White's main move, and it breaks the pin, so we will now eliminate the knight attacking our queen.

rn2k2r/pbp2ppp/1p2pn2/3q4/3P4/2PB1N2/P1P.text: Recapturing. And now Black has the option of Nbd7 or Qh5. We prefer to develop another piece instead of moving the queen yet again unprovoked.

rnbqkbnr/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/5N2/PPP2P.text: White develops a piece and supports d4. We will fianchetto our light-squared bishop, applying pressure to e4.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/4p3/8/3PP3/8/PPP2PPP/R.text: White pushes another central pawn. We will prepare to fianchetto our bishop.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
This is the third and final study of this chapter. We'll go over the variations that may arise after 6. Qe2. Master them, and you'll master the system!

Let's play 1...e6.

2rq1rk1/1b1nbppp/1pn1p3/p2pP3/P2P4/3BBN1.text: We place our rook on the open file before considering a knight jump to b4. Things look promising for Black.

r2q1rk1/1b1nbppp/1pn1p3/p1ppP3/P2P4/2PBB.text:
This puts a stop to any further queenside pawn expansion by us.

But now an exchange of pawns will lead to a potential knight outpost on b4!

r2q1rk1/pb1nbppp/1pn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/2PBBN1.text:
White likes this move in these structures. It can be seen as a useful waiting move.

We will gain queenside space and make the b4 expansion idea harder for White!

r2qk2r/p2nbp1p/bpn1p3/2ppP1p1/3P2P1/P1P2.text:
If White doesn't like the idea of us playing g4 ourselves...

We can push forward with h5, forcing the issue on the kingside.

r2qk2r/p2nbp2/bpn1p3/2ppP1pp/3P2P1/P1P2N.text: White defends the pawn, but in the process they have weakened their king's position.

r2qk2r/p2nbppp/bpn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/P1P2N2/1.text:
White continues to develop their pieces.

In response, we play a very creative idea! The queenside is somewhat locked. If cxd4, White could recapture with the c-pawn and have two pawns in the center.
 
As Black, we will opt for expanding on the kingside, and activating our rook through that expansion.

r2qkb1r/p4ppp/npn1p3/2ppP3/1P1P4/P1P2N2/.text:
The move prepared by a3. Watch out, a pawn fork of the knights is now threatened!

Therefore we will retreat the a6-knight.

rn1q1rk1/pb2bppp/1pn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/2PBBN2.text:
White places the rook on a more active square, and gives the bishop the possibility of retreating to c2 or b1 if a trade is offered.

We will develop our last minor piece, and bring it where it supports the center, in particular our c5-pawn.

rn1qk2r/p3bppp/1p2p3/nPppP3/3P4/P1P1BN2/.text: We prepare castling while covering the g5 square. White is a touch weak on the light squares on the queenside.

rn1qk2r/p3bppp/bpn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/P1P2N2/1.text:
White prepares a future b4 queenside expansion.

In reply, we bring our last undeveloped minor piece into the game.

rn1qk2r/pb2bppp/1pn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/2PBBN2/.text: White develops their final minor piece, and we will castle.

rn1qkb1r/p4ppp/1p2p3/nPppP3/3P4/P1P1BN2/.text: White develops with Be3, supporting the center.

rn1qkb1r/p4ppp/1pn1p3/1PppP3/3P4/P1P2N2/.text: b5 is played anyway, attacking the other knight, which we will deploy to a5, eyeing the outpost on c4.

rn1qkb1r/p4ppp/Bpn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/P1P2N2/1.text: White didn't have the option of retreating to c2 because the d3-bishop is pinned to the rook. Thus the bishops are exchanged.

rn1qkb1r/p4ppp/bpn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/2P2N2/PP.text:
A retreating move, preserving the bishop, made possible because of 8.Re1.

We continue with a developing move which also controls g5 and prepares castling.

rn1qkb1r/pb2nppp/1p2p3/2ppP3/3P4/2PB1N2/.text: Castling the king into safety. We will continue our plan with the e7-knight.

rn1qkb1r/pb3ppp/1pn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/2PB1N2/.text:
One major option is 8.Re1, where White supports their center, and places the rook on a more active file. 

Also, White can retain the bishops when a trade is offered with Ba6 - as we shall see.

rn1qkb1r/pb3ppp/1pn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/2PBBN2/.text: White develops with Be3, supporting the center. In response we will prepare to castle by playing Be7.

rn1qkb1r/pb3ppp/1pn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/P1PB1N2.text:
In this variation, the rook is left on f1. White decides to prepare b4 as rapidly as possible. 

However, since the rook is still on f1, the bishop trade offer on a6 will enforce the removal of the light-squared bishops.

rn1qkbnr/pb3ppp/1p2p3/2ppP3/3P4/2PB1N2/P.text:
Supporting the center.

We will play Ne7. Our idea to put the e7-knight on c6, and use the other knight on b8 to support a trade of the light-squared bishops with Ba6.

rn1qkbnr/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/3P4/3B1N2/PP.text:
By far White's most popular response is to advance the pawn, gaining space and reducing the central pressure. 

We will once again strike at the center! It's important to move our c-pawn before developing a knight to c6.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/3B1N2/PPP.text: White develops the knight. We will stake our claim to the center with ...d5.

rnbqkbnr/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/3B4/PPP2P.text:
White might go 3.Nf3 first, but it's the same idea if they go 4.Bd3 after. 

3.Bd3 supports e4. 

We will continue by fianchettoing the bishop, targeting the e4-pawn.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/4p3/8/3PP3/8/PPP2PPP/R.text: A second pawn joins the center, and we prepare the fianchetto.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
Welcome to Chapter 2! This chapter deals with e4/d4, but instead of White supporting them with both knights, the pawns will be supported by a Nf3 and Bd3 configuration.

Let's play 1...e6.

r2q1r2/pbp2pk1/1pn1pn1p/6p1/2PP4/P1N2NP1.text: Retreating the bishop ensures that d4 is now defended adequately.

r2q1r2/pbp2pk1/1pn1pn1p/8/2PP2p1/P1N2NP1.text: But we can kick the knight away, with the idea of removing the defender of d4. White has questions to answer!

r2q1rk1/pbp1bppp/1p2pn2/4P1B1/2P5/2NB4/P.text:
White recaptures.

We will fall back, eyeing e5 and c5, while offering a bishop exchange.

r2q1rk1/pbp1bppp/1pn1pn2/8/2PP1B2/P1NB1N.text:
This move keeps the knight from b4. White is not currently concerned about the d-pawn, because there are tricks with a Bxh7 discovery.

We will offer to trade off the strong bishop on f4.

r2q1rk1/pbp2p2/1pn1pn1p/6p1/2PP4/P1NB1NP.text:
Recapturing towards the center. We will now put our king on a safer square, one where there are no tricks available to the d3-bishop. 

This means we will finally be threatening to capture twice on d4. With the king still on g8, the sequence of captures on d4 would result in us losing our queen to Bh7+ at the end of the line. With the king on g7, Bh7 is no longer check.

r2q1rk1/pbp2p2/1pnbpn1p/6p1/2PP4/P1NB1NB.text: White retreats, and we will finally trade bishops.

r2q1rk1/pbp2pp1/1pnbpn1p/8/2PP3B/P1NB1N2.text: Choosing to maintain the pin, and we will reply by harassing the bishop and breaking the pin.

r2q1rk1/pbp2ppp/1pnbpn2/6B1/2PP4/P1NB1N2.text:
Bg5 choosing to pin the knight and not trade. White perceives that we are slightly cramped, so it makes sense for them to keep pieces on.

We will now target the bishop with our pawns.

r2q1rk1/pbpnBppp/1p2p3/4P3/2P5/2NB4/PP3P.text: White exchanges bishops, and we will recapture.

r2q1rk1/pbpnbppp/1p2pn2/4N1B1/2PP4/2NB4/.text: Jumping into the center. We will exchange off the dominating knight.

r4rk1/1bpn1pp1/1p2p3/p3P1p1/1PP5/2NBR3/P.text: Attacking b4! The idea is that c5 is a strong outpost for the knight, so if Black can remove the b4 pawn, the knight will gain access.

r4rk1/pbpn1pp1/1p2p2p/4P1Q1/2P5/2NBR3/PP.text: Accepting the trade, and we recapture.

r4rk1/pbpnqpp1/1p2p2p/4P2Q/2P5/2NBR3/PP3.text:
Bringing another piece into the mix.

Another purpose of h6! Black can offer a queen trade here to neutralize the attack.

r4rk1/pbpnqppp/1p2p3/4P2Q/2P5/2NB4/PP3PP.text:
Converging on h7. Whatever you do, don't blunder mate!

We will neutralize the threat by playing h6.

rn1q1rk1/pbp1bppp/1p2pn2/6B1/2PP4/2NB1N2.text: One option is to develop the bishop to g5. We will develop our b8-knight, supporting its partner on f6.

rn1q1rk1/pbp1bppp/1p2pn2/6B1/3P4/2NB1N2/.text: Now we get the king to safety. Play might continue with developing the last minor piece and pushing c7-c5.

rn1q1rk1/pbp1bppp/1p2pn2/8/2PP1B2/2NB1N2.text: Alternatively, White can develop the bishop to f4. We will continue by developing and placing pressure on d4.

rn1qk2r/pbp1bppp/1p2pn2/6B1/3P4/2NB1N2/P.text: Qe2 connects the rooks and looks down the more active e-file.

rn1qk2r/pbp1bppp/1p2pn2/8/2PP4/2NB1N2/PP.text: White places their rook actively on a semi-open file. We will castle into safety.

rn1qkb1r/pbp2ppp/1p2pn2/6B1/3P4/2NB1N2/P.text:
This is the most popular continuation, pinning the knight.

We will reply with the natural ...Be7, breaking the pin.

rn1qkb1r/pbp2ppp/1p2pn2/8/2PP4/2NB1N2/PP.text: White develops their other knight. We will bring our f8-bishop out, and get ready to castle.

rn1qkbnr/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3P4/3P4/3B1N2/PPP.text:
This is the second most popular choice by White. Let's explore what happens.

We will develop the queen! Additionally, we leave the diagonal open for our bishop.

rn1qkbnr/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/8/2PP4/3B1N2/PP3P.text:
Getting the king to safety.

We will develop our king's knight, and stake a claim to the central light squares.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/3B1N2/PPP.text:
White develops the knight. 

We will push in the center.

rn2kb1r/pbp2ppp/1p2pn2/3q4/3P4/2NB1N2/PP.text: Attacking our queen! We will retreat to d8.

rn2kbnr/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3q4/2PP4/3B1N2/PP3.text: Attacking the queen! We will retreat to d8.

rn2kbnr/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3q4/3P4/3B1N2/PPP2.text: White castles into safety. We will develop the knight, building control over the central light squares.

rnbqkbnr/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/3B4/PPP2P.text:
White might go 3.Nf3 first, but it's the same idea if they go 4.Bd3 after. 

3.Bd3 supports e4. 

We fianchetto our bishop, putting pressure on e4.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/4p3/8/3PP3/8/PPP2PPP/R.text: A second pawn joins the center, and we will prepare our fianchetto.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
In this study, we'll analyze what happens after we play 4...d5 and White decides to take. It's a very natural response, so let's take a look at it!

As before we continue with e6 and b6.

lessons.title: White Setups with Bd3 and Nd2, Ne2

2r1kb1r/p1qn1ppp/bp2p3/n2pP3/3P4/1P2BN2/.text: We converge strongly on the c-file! b3 also weakened a3, so now our bishop can go there!

2rqkb1r/p2n1ppp/bp2p3/n2pP3/3P4/1P2BN2/P.text: And if White wants to defend against the knight jump?

2rqkb1r/p2n1ppp/bpn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/2P1BN2/.text:
The knight makes more sense here, supporting d4 and also allowing the queen to have sight of d4.

Let's exchange on d4, opening the file for our rook.

2rqkb1r/p2n1ppp/bpn1p3/3pP3/3P4/4BN2/PPB.text:
Recapturing and defending e5.

We play Na5, with the idea of jumping to the outpost on c4 and attacking both the e3-bishop and the pawn on b2.

r2q1rk1/p2pbppp/np2pn2/8/3PP3/P4N2/1P1N1.text: We castle into safety. We can play to occupy the open c-file.

r2qk1nr/pb3p1p/1pn1p1p1/2bpP3/5NQ1/2NB4/.text: White places their rook on a more active square, and supports their pawn on e5.

r2qk1nr/pb3ppp/1pn1p3/2bpP3/5NQ1/2NB4/PP.text: White develops their queen, attacking g7. We will push the g-pawn forward, constructing a defensive shield of pawns.

r2qk2r/p2pbppp/np2pn2/8/3PP3/P4N2/1P1N1P.text: White covers the b4 square, preventing our knight from arriving there.

r2qk2r/pb2np1p/1pn1p1p1/2bpP3/5NQ1/2NB4/.text: We develop the knight. The plan is to go ...a6, to prevent Nb5 jumps, and we can expand further with ...b5 next.

r2qkb1r/p2n1ppp/bpn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/2P1B3/P.text:
White also develops.

We place the rook on c8, preparing to activate it in the near future when we open the c-file.

r2qkb1r/pb1n1p1p/4p1p1/1NppPn2/5P2/1P1B2.text: And we defend! Our knight reaches a nice outpost that in turn stops the kingside expansion and offers a trade which would leave us with a very solid central pawn mass if White accepts.

r2qkb1r/pb1nnp1p/4p1p1/1NppP3/5P2/1P1B2N.text: With the crude idea of giving a checkmate on d6!

r2qkb1r/pb1nnppp/4p3/2ppP3/5P2/1PNB2N1/P.text:
Expanding on the kingside!

We will need to cut across White's plan by playing ...g6.

r2qkbnr/pb3ppp/1pn1p3/2PpP3/5N2/2NB4/PPP.text: If White chooses to resolve the tension, we will recapture with the bishop.

r2qkbnr/pb3ppp/1pn1p3/2ppP2Q/3P1N2/2NB4/.text:
White could try this venomous move, threatening to take on e6, as the f-pawn is pinned.

We will defend e6 with our queen.

r3k1nr/pb1q1p1p/1pn1p1p1/2bpP3/5N2/2NB3Q.text: And we develop the bishop. As you can see, castling queenside is available to us in the next move.

r3kbnr/pb1q1p1p/1pn1p1p1/2PpP3/5N2/2NB3Q.text: Choosing to stay on the kingside, applying pressure there.

r3kbnr/pb1q1ppp/1pn1p3/2PpP2Q/5N2/2NB4/P.text: White can play this move, reducing the pressure on d4. We will reply by pushing the queen away before recapturing.

rn1qk2r/p2pbppp/Bp2pn2/8/3PP3/5N2/PP1N1P.text:
The trade is accepted. White has little choice, because if the bishop retreated, the f1-rook would be en prise.

We recapture.

rn1qk2r/pb1pbppp/1p2pn2/8/3PP3/3B1N2/PP1.text:
Getting the king to safety.

We offer the bishop trade. White's bishop is pointing dangerously at the kingside.

rn1qkb1r/p4ppp/bpn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/2P1B3/PP.text:
Rejecting the trade. Our bishop is well-placed on that diagonal.

We continue to develop.

rn1qkb1r/pb1p1ppp/1p2pn2/2p5/3PP3/2PB1N2.text:
Developing the knight and supporting the center.

We exchange on d4.

rn1qkb1r/pb1p1ppp/1p2pn2/8/3PP3/3B1N2/PP.text:
White recaptures with the pawn. If White recaptures with a piece, this helps Black, due to the diminished central presence.

We will develop our bishop and prepare to castle kingside.

rn1qkb1r/pb2nppp/1p2p3/2ppP3/3P4/2PB4/PP.text:
White castles into safety.

We will reply with Nec6, getting the knight to a better square and freeing our dark-squared bishop.

rn1qkb1r/pb2nppp/4p3/2ppP3/8/1PNB2N1/P1P.text:
White opens up lines for their queen, and gives themselves the option of pushing forward with the f-pawn.

We will develop our other knight.

rn1qkb1r/pb3ppp/1pn1p3/2ppP3/3P4/2PBB3/P.text:
This is a sound move, developing and supporting the center.

We will offer a trade of bishops. If White rejects, there'll be a pin on the knight on e2.

rn1qkb1r/pbp2ppp/1p2pn2/3pP3/3P4/2NB4/PP.text: White chooses to take space, attacking our knight on f6. We will retreat the knight, planning to later redeploy it to e7.

rn1qkb1r/pbpp1ppp/1p2pn2/8/3PP3/2NB4/PPP.text:
White develops another knight, supporting their c3-knight and the d4-pawn.

We will push in the center.

rn1qkbnr/pb1p1ppp/1p2p3/2p5/3PP3/2PB4/PP.text:
White plays c3, supporting d4.

We will develop our king's knight, attacking more forces to the attack on e4.

rn1qkbnr/pb3ppp/1p2p3/2PpP3/8/2NB4/PPP1N.text: Alternatively, White might simply resolve the tension. In this case, we will recapture towards the center, controlling more squares.

rn1qkbnr/pb3ppp/1p2p3/2ppP3/3P1N2/2NB4/P.text:
A very aggressive move! d4 isn't really a free pawn. White can recover it later with Nce2.

With that in mind, we prefer to continue by putting pressure on d4 by developing the b8-knight.

rn1qkbnr/pb3ppp/1p2p3/2ppP3/3P4/2PB4/PP2.text:
White defends their pawn chain with the c-pawn.

We will play Ne7, and we can utilize ideas from Chapter 2, like bringing the e-knight to c6, and offering the bishop trade on a6.

rn1qkbnr/pb3ppp/4p3/2ppP3/8/1PNB4/P1P1NP.text: White prevents c4, which would have trapped the bishop on d3. We will develop our king's knight.

rn1qkbnr/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/3P4/2NB4/PPP.text: White castles the king into safety, and we will strike at the center with c5.

rn1qkbnr/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/3P4/3B4/PPP1.text:
White pushes forward, gaining space.

We will strike at the base of the pawn chain.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/2NB4/PPP2.text: White develops, also supporting e4. We will develop our king's knight and continue to eye the e4-pawn.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/3B4/PPP1N.text:
Another option would be this move, developing another knight and supporting d4. 

We will strike at the center!

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/3B4/PPPN1.text:
White can develop with this move, also supporting e4. 

We will play to undermine the white center.

rnbqkbnr/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/3B4/PPP2P.text:
The bishop arrives behind the pawns, supporting e4.

We will fianchetto our bishop, aiming at the center.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/4p3/8/3PP3/8/PPP2PPP/R.text:
Establishing a second central pawn.

And we will continue with our fianchetto system.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
In this study we start off with variations where White develops the light-squared bishop first, defending the e4 pawn. The point will be to analyze the various knight moves available to White in the 4th move, which we haven't looked at yet.

Let's continue with 1...e6.

r2qk2r/pbp2ppp/1pnbp3/8/2PP1B2/P4N2/1P3P.text: We'll recapture, developing our bishop and offering a trade. We're comfortable here, with a powerful bishop on b7.

r2qkb1r/p2n1ppp/2b1p3/2ppP3/2P5/P2B1N2/2.text: We develop the last queenside piece. After a future ...Be7, we'll castle into safety, with a solid position.

r2qkb1r/pb3ppp/1pn1p3/1BppPn2/3P4/2N1BP2.text: We place the white center under pressure.

r2qkbnr/pb3ppp/1pn1p3/1BppP3/3P4/2N1BP2/.text:
White tries to neutralize the pressure by pinning our attacker.

We support our knight on c6. The e7-knight can go to f5 next move, attacking d4 and e3 as well!

rn1q1rk1/pb1pbppp/4pn2/2p5/4P3/2NBBN2/PP.text: We do likewise. We have no problems as we emerge from the opening.

rn1qk1nr/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/3P4/4b3/2B2N2/PP.text: White pushes d5. This tricky move opens up an attack on g7! Look at the bishop! If g7 falls, so will the rook behind it!

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1b1PP3/2N2N2/P.text:
This is a natural move, breaking the pin! But is that a free pawn we see?

We will take on c3, removing the defender.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/2B2N2/PPP.text:
White recaptures with the bishop.

Now we can take on e4.

rn1qk1nr/pbppbppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/3BBN2/PPP.text:
White develops, supporting the center.

We will develop, with our pieces converging on e4.

rn1qk2r/p1pp1ppp/1p2pn2/3P4/4b3/2B2N2/PP.text: We block the diagonal by developing a piece and we are a healthy pawn up.

rn1qk2r/pb1p1ppp/1p2pn2/8/1b1PPP2/2NB4/P.text:
Since the knight is pinned, White defends the e-pawn further with Qe2.

We will continue to challenge the center, this time by pushing our d-pawn.

rn1qk2r/pb1pbppp/1p2pn2/2P5/4P3/2NBBN2/P.text: White releases the tension, and we will capture towards the center with the b-pawn, exerting control over d4.

rn1qk2r/pb3ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/1b1PnP2/2NB4/P.text: We jump into the center, since our knight is sufficiently supported. We are attacking c3. Furthermore, if white takes, they'll relinquish their light-square bishop, and our queen will gain a tempo on the d4 pawn.

rn1qk2r/pb3ppp/1p2pn2/3pP3/1b1P1P2/2NB4/.text: White pushes the pawn and attacks our knight!

rn1qk2r/pbppbppp/1p2pn2/8/3PP3/2NBBN2/PP.text:
White adds a defender to e4.
It seems White studied a book on opening principles, as the pieces are all developed supporting the center!

However, we are familiar with the principles of undermining a center!

rn1qkb1r/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/3bP3/2PP4/P7/1P3.text:
White can attack our bishop.

We will retreat it back to its natural home on b7.

rn1qkb1r/p4ppp/2b1p3/2ppP3/2P5/P2B1N2/2P.text: White advances c4, with the option of undoubling their c-pawns.

rn1qkb1r/pb1p1ppp/1p2pn2/2p5/3PP3/P1NB1N.text:
White develops, defending d4.

We will again put pressure on the center, this time by pushing d5.

rn1qkb1r/pb1p1ppp/1p2pn2/8/3PPP2/2NB4/PP.text:
White defends e4.

We will apply further pressure by pinning the knight.

rn1qkb1r/pb3ppp/1p2p3/2PpP3/4n3/P1NB1N2/.text:
White releases the pressure in the center.

We will play an intermezzo, exchanging knights and doubling White's pawns.

rn1qkb1r/pb3ppp/1p2p3/2PpP3/8/P1PB1N2/2P.text:
White of course recaptures.

We will capture towards the center, covering the d4 and b4 squares.

rn1qkb1r/pb3ppp/1p2p3/2pN4/3P4/P2B1N2/1P.text:
White decides to exchange.

We recapture with our queen, bringing it to an aggressive central location.

rn1qkb1r/pb3ppp/1p2pn2/2pP4/3P4/P1NB1N2/.text:
White decides to release the tension.

We will recapture with our knight, not with the pawn, which would voluntarily block our light-square bishop.

rn1qkb1r/pb3ppp/1p2pn2/2ppP3/3P4/P1NB1N2.text:
White advances, gaining space and attacking our knight.

We jump into the center, supported by the d5-pawn and our bishop on b7.

rn1qkb1r/pb3ppp/4p3/2ppP3/8/P1PB1N2/2P2P.text:
The rook moves to b-the open file, attacking our bishop.

We will simply move it to c6.

rn1qkb1r/pbp2ppp/1p1pp3/4P3/2PP1B2/P4N2/.text:
White supports e5.

We will continue increasing the pressure.

rn1qkb1r/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/3NP3/3P4/P7/1PP2.text:
That is why more often than not White chooses to take.

We will recapture with the bishop, keeping the long diagonal open.

rn1qkb1r/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/4P3/2PP4/P4N2/1P.text:
White develops, supporting their center.

We will reply with d6, aiming to break up the strong pawn center.

rn1qkb1r/pbpp1ppp/1p2pn2/4P3/3P4/P1N5/1P.text:
White may elect to push the pawn. This is a very natural continuation, so, while it isn't the most popular, it's still useful for us to get to know.

We will jump into the center and offer a trade. We're threatening to double White's pawns!

rn1qkb1r/pbpp1ppp/1p2pn2/8/3PP3/P1NB4/1P.text:
White defends e4.

Let's strike at the center with c5!

rn1qkbnr/pb1p1ppp/1p2p3/2p5/3PPP2/2PB4/P.text:
White wants to hold on to the center, naturally.

We will exchange on d4.

rn1qkbnr/pb1p1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PPP2/3B4/PP4P.text:
White recaptures.

We will place further pressure on the center by developing our g8-knight.

rn1qkbnr/pb3ppp/1p2p3/2ppP3/3P4/2N1BP2/P.text:
White develops their bishop, supporting d4.

We will continue to pressurize the d-pawn.

rn1qkbnr/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3pP3/3P4/2N2P2/PP.text:
White closes off the center. The f-pawn looks misplaced, blocking the natural development square of the g1-knight.

We will break with c5.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/2N2N2/PPP.text:
White defends e4. Two knights, developing as normal.

We will bring our king's bishop out, and pin the knight, thus placing pressure on e4 once more.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/2N2P2/PPP.text:
How about this solution? White just supports e4 with another pawn!

We will push d5, striking at the white center.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/3BB3/PPP2.text:
White can opt for a center supported by their two bishops.
Remember that whenever the white knight doesn't develop to c3, we won't play Bb4 as there will be nothing to pin.

Therefore we develop the bishop on e7, with the idea of castling kingside.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/P1N5/1PP2.text:
With a3, White prevents us from playing our traditional Bb4 pinning the knight on c3. The knight, therefore, will stay supporting e4, unbothered.

Let's develop and continue attacking e4.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PPP2/3B4/PPP3.text:
White defends the e-pawn.

White hasn't placed a knight on c3, therefore there's no point in playing Bb4 next move, as white could simply play c3.

With that in mind, we will strike at the center with the c-pawn instead.

rn2k2r/pb2bppp/3qp3/2p5/2P5/P2B1N2/1P3PP.text: We prepare to castle, too. We have a healthy position, with clear open lines for our pieces.

rn2kb1r/pb3ppp/1p1qp3/2P5/2P5/P2B1N2/1P3.text:
White again chooses to liquidate.

We will recapture towards the center.

rn2kb1r/pb3ppp/1p2p3/2pq4/2PP4/P2B1N2/1P.text:
Our queen is attacked!

We retreat, keeping an eye on the f4-square. White can no longer develop their dark-squared bishop there.

rnbqkbnr/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/2N5/PPP2P.text:
Supporting e4. This is a very natural move. Nothing odd here.

We will continue with our normal fianchetto.

rnbqkbnr/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/3B4/PPP2P.text:
White may decide to support e4 like this. Nothing we haven't seen before, should White choose to go 4.Nf3 in the next move. But what if they continue with a different idea?

In the meantime, we fianchetto our bishop.

rnbqkbnr/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PP3/5N2/PPP2P.text:
What if White continues in a regular fashion as we have seen before, by developing a knight supporting the center?

As usual, we fianchetto our bishop, attacking the pawn on e4.

rnbqkbnr/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/8/3PPP2/8/PPP3PP.text:
White might have learned that having a large center is good! In this case, we must remember that large centers can be attacked with pawns.

We begin our counterstrike by fianchettoing.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/4p3/8/3PP3/8/PPP2PPP/R.text:
A second central pawn push. Nothing out of the ordinary yet.

We will prepare to fianchetto.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
This study will cover things we don't expect to see after the common 1.e4 e6 2.d4 b6. 

What if White plays moves like 3.f4, or 3.Nc3 and 4.a3? Well, study this chapter, and you'll be able to deal with some off-beat approaches by White.

4k2r/p1prn1pp/1p3q2/8/2P1Q3/2P2N2/P4PPP/.text: We just recapture. We have a safer king and better piece development, while White's c-pawns are very weak.

r2q1rk1/pbp3pp/1p6/n2P1n2/Q4B2/2P2P2/P5P.text:
And we sidestep, opening our bishop up to attack the pawn. While we're in no rush to take it since our bishop would end up in a precarious situation, White still has to be careful.

We have five developed pieces, whereas white only has 3. The defenses of the White king are also somewhat scattered.

r2q1rk1/pbp3pp/1pn5/3P1n2/Q4B2/2P2P2/P5P.text: White captures our pawn, attacking our knight.

r2q1rk1/pbpn2pp/1p6/5n2/1bPP1B2/2N2P2/PP.text:
White might have anxiety because they notice they're down in development. Also, they might try to block the e-file to protect their king.

We will play a queen check, and probe at the enemy king.

r2qk1nr/pbp3pp/1pnpp3/4Pp2/1bPP4/2N1BP2/.text: And we undermine the center. White may well find that they have over-extended.

r2qk1nr/pbpp2pp/1pn1p3/4Pp2/1bPP4/2N1BP2.text: They develop the bishop, supporting d4.

r2qk2r/pbp3pp/1pn1p3/3P1n2/Q1P2B2/2P2P2/.text: White recaptures, and we'll capture on d5.

r2qk2r/pbp3pp/1pn1p3/3P1n2/QbP2B2/2N2P2/.text:
White pushes, attacking our knight.

We make it easier to fend off the attack by removing a defender of d5.

r2qk2r/pbp3pp/1pn5/3p1n2/Q1P2B2/2P2P2/P5.text:
White castles, pinning our pawn to the queen!

But we will castle into safety, and unpin the c6-knight.

r2qk2r/pbpn2pp/1p6/5n2/1bPP1B2/2N2P2/PP4.text:
White develops a piece (at last).

And we complete our development by castling (all we need to do now is connect rooks).

r3k1nr/p1ppq1pp/1pn1p3/6B1/2PPQ3/2P2N2/P.text:
Developing the bishop, attacking the queen!

We block the attack with our other knight, attacking the White queen.

r3k2r/p1pp2pp/1pn1pq2/3P4/2P1Q3/2P2N2/P4.text:
A clever move! Attacking our knight, trying to remove it from c6 to unleash an attack on our a8-rook.

We will move the knight to e7, and sacrifice a pawn.

r3k2r/p1ppn1pp/1p2Pq2/8/2P1Q3/2P2N2/P4PP.text:
White opens up the attack on our rook! We don't have time to recapture.

We will just move the rook instead, protecting d7.

r3k2r/p1ppq1pp/1pn1pB2/8/2PPQ3/2P2N2/P4P.text: White snaps off the knight, and we recapture with the queen.

r3k2r/p1ppq1pp/1pn1pn2/8/2PPQ3/2P1BN2/P4.text: Nf6 allows us to develop with a tempo.

r4rk1/p1pn2pp/1p6/5n1q/1bPP1B2/2N2bP1/PP.text: But we can still capture the pawn! We have a very promising position.

r4rk1/pbpn2pp/1p6/5n2/1bPP1B1q/2N2PP1/PP.text:
With g3, White blocks the check.

We drop back with tempo, attacking f3.

rn1q1rk1/pbp3pp/1p2p3/5n2/1bPP1B2/2N2P2/.text:
But we're so far ahead that our king gets to safety, while White's is still stuck in the middle of the board.

We'll develop our queenside pieces, connect the rooks and put pressure on d4.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/3P4/1bP1P3/2N5/P.text: d5 blocks the attack on e4! Our bishop now faces the pawn on d5, and its scope is blunted. We will capture on c3, doubling White's pawns.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1bPPP3/2N2P2/P.text:
f3 is a sound move, defending the e4 pawn with another pawn.

But we can still counter it with f5!

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1bPPP3/2N5/PPQ.text: White can choose to defend e4 this way. We will bring out our queen, attacking e4 again.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1bPPP3/2NB4/PP.text: This is the main line, defending e4.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/4Pp2/1bPP4/2N2P2/.text:
White might choose to advance the pawn.

We will develop our queen's knight. Our development is ahead of White's.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5P2/1bPP4/2N2P2/P.text:
White takes, and thus gets their pawn removed from the center. This is good. In the resulting positions, you'll notice, White's center looks less impressive than a few moves ago.

We will reply with the sharp ...Nh6, applying pressure on f5, with the idea of Qh4+ if the bishop takes our knight on h6.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5p2/1bPPP3/2NB4/P.text:
We proceed by undermining the center! Note that White cannot take because the g2-pawn would become loose.

The resulting variations that can occur after 5...f5 will be analyzed in the next study. For now, just remember the basic moves to get here!

rn1qk2r/pbp3pp/1p2p3/5n2/1bPP1B2/2N2P2/P.text: White tries to catch up in development.

rn1qk2r/pbp3pp/1p2p3/5n2/QbPP1B2/2N2P2/P.text:
White could opt to check us, forking our king and bishop.

We will interpose our b8-knight and protect the bishop.

rn1qk2r/pbpP2pp/1p6/5n2/1bPP4/2N2P2/PP4P.text:
Other players choose to gobble up another pawn.

We will recapture, and develop another minor piece. We play in gambit style!

rn1qk2r/pbpp2pp/1p2P2n/8/1bPP4/2N2P2/PP4.text:
White can choose to pawn grab.

We'll choose to improve our pieces with Nf5! You'll notice we now threaten Qh4+ because our knight covers g3.

rn1qk2r/pbpp2pp/1p2P3/5n2/1bPP1B2/2N2P2/.text:
Master level players typically develop another piece, as they're behind in development. This move also adds another defender to the g3 square.

After that, we can just recapture the pawn, supporting our active knight on f5.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/2PPP3/2N5/PP3P.text:
White gains space by putting another pawn in the center! An impressive center that we'll have fun undermining.

We begin by pinning the knight, thus loosening e4.

This introduces the first checkpoint of our study. White has four concrete responses they can throw at us.

rn1qkbnr/pbpppppp/1p6/8/2PP4/2N5/PP2PPPP.text:
White develops the knight to c3, which controls d5 and e4.

Now we prepare to counter on the light-squares with ...e6, controlling d5. This move additionally opens up our dark-squared bishop.

rn2k1nr/p1ppq1pp/1p2p3/5p2/2PPB3/2P2N2/P.text: White removes our strong bishop, and we recapture.

rn2k1nr/p1ppq1pp/1p2p3/8/2PPQ3/2P2N2/P4P.text:
White regains the pawn, hitting the rook on a8.

We will develop our queen's knight, blocking the attack.

rn2k1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1bPPP2q/2NB4/PP.text:
White, therefore, adds another defender.

We will strike at the center with ...f5, noting that the g-pawn is loose if White captures on f5.

rn2k1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5p2/1bPPP2q/2NB1N2.text:
Nf3 gains a tempo on our queen.

Before we move the queen to safety, we will insert the capture on c3, with check.

rn2k1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5p2/2PPP1q1/2QB1N2.text:
White gets to safety.

In the resulting position, we can capture on e4, challenging White to find the correct moves to not lose material.

rn2k1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5p2/2PPP2q/2bB1N2/.text:
The cunning Kf1 is possible here, defending g2 and getting out of the pin, while maintaining an attack on both the queen on h4 and the bishop on c3.

We will retreat to the safety of e7.

rn2k1nr/pbppq1pp/1p2p3/5p2/2PPP3/2PB1N2/.text:
White recaptures with the b-pawn, leaving the queen in the defense of e4.

We will reply by exchanging in the center.

rn2k1nr/pbppqppp/1p2p3/3P4/2P1P3/2P5/P4P.text:
Now we develop the queen on an active square, covering a3 before a bishop chooses to make its way there.

Additionally, we're opposing the king with our queen, so if we can take exd5 next move, our queen will have an open attack on the undefended e4 pawn!

rnbqkbnr/p1pppppp/1p6/8/2PP4/8/PP2PPPP/R.text:
This move brings out another pawn which controls the central d5 square.

We proceed with our plan to fianchetto.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/3P4/8/PPP1PPPP/RNB.text:
Welcome! In this chapter, we'll learn about what happens when White opens with 1.d4, and then proceeds to arrange a large center with c4 and e4. 

You'll also see that White supports this center with a piece like Nc3 or Bd3.

This time, we'll start off with 1...b6.

4rrk1/p1p1n1pp/1p1pp3/5q2/P1PP4/2P2N2/1Q.text: Seeking to maybe go a5 and open up a line for the a1-rook. We continue to relocate the knight on the kingside.

4rrk1/p1p3pp/1p1pp1n1/1Q3q2/P1PP4/2P2N2/.text:
White now wants a queen trade to improve their structure!

We won't cooperate. We play c5, blocking the line between the opposing queens.

4rrk1/p1p3pp/1pnpp3/5q2/2PP4/2P2N2/PQ3PP.text:
White maneuvers the queen around, planning to challenge our queen with a future Qb5.

We bring our knight to the kingside.

4rrk1/p1pp2pp/1pn1p3/5q2/2PP4/2P2N2/P3QP.text:
White seeks to prevent e5.

We will support it by playing ...d6.

4rrk1/p5pp/1p1pp1n1/2p2q2/P1PP4/2P2N2/5P.text:
White continues to offer a queen trade. Our presence on the kingside has got stronger over the past few moves.

We will retain queens, because we are now playing for the attack.

4rrk1/p5pp/1p1pp1n1/2p4q/P1PPQ3/2P2N2/5P.text: Trying to control squares on the kingside.

4rrk1/p5pp/1p1pp3/2p4q/P1PPQn2/2P2N2/5PP.text: Our knight becomes a monster on f4! Our rook on f8 also looks down the file menacingly! White is very much on the defensive.

r2q1Rk1/pbpp2pp/1pn1p3/8/1bPPP1n1/2NB4/P.text:
White seeks to alleviate the tension...

We recapture and threaten to infiltrate with the queen!

r2q1n1r/pbp2kpp/1p2pn2/6B1/2PP1N1Q/2PB4/.text: We fall back, defending with the knight. We've survived the attack, and White is down material.

r2q1rk1/pbpn2pp/1p1p1n2/3Pp3/2P5/2P1BBN1.text: The bishop goes to e3, and we prepare to line up our major pieces on the half-open f-file.

r2q1rk1/pbpp2pp/1pn1pn2/8/1bPPP3/2NB4/PP.text:
White can play the very natural move of castling.

We will jump our knight into action on g4! The e2-knight is not best placed defensively.

r2q2k1/pbpn1rpp/1p1p1n2/3Pp3/2P5/2P1BBN1.text: The queen is developed onto a better diagonal.

r2q3r/pbpn1kpp/1p2pn2/6B1/2PP1N1Q/2PB4/P.text: White tries piling up on e6.

r2qk2r/pbpp2pp/1pn1pn2/5p2/1bPPP3/2NB1P2.text:
The knight develops to e2, supporting their comrade on c3.

We will soften up the white center by exchanging pawns on e4.

r2qk2r/pbpp2pp/1pn1pn2/8/1bPPP3/2NB4/PPQ.text:
White recaptures, and we will castle, placing our rook on the open f-file.

If White wants to try 9...0-0 10.e5 to win h7, they may have trouble defending their king after 10.Ng4.

r3k2r/p1pp3p/1pn1pqp1/8/1bPPQ3/2N2N2/PP3.text:
White develops the knight and defends d4.

We will damage White's pawn structure and argue that we are a touch better.

r4qk1/pbpn1rpp/1p1p1n2/3Pp3/2P5/2P1BBN1/.text: We double major pieces on the f-file. We have a promising position. White's bishops don't have much scope, and our knights will prove flexible.

r4qk1/pbpp2pp/1pn1p3/8/1bPPP1n1/3B4/PPQ1.text: It was vital to cover the f2 entry point.

r4rk1/p1pp2pp/1pn1p3/5q2/2PP4/2P2N2/P3QP.text: Choosing to retain the queens. We will activate our queen's rook, with a potential ...e5 pawn push in mind.

r4rk1/p1pp2pp/1pn1pq2/8/1bPPQ3/2N2N2/PP3.text: White gets their king into safety, and we will capture on c3, doubling their pawns.

r4rk1/p1pp2pp/1pn1pq2/8/2PPQ3/2P2N2/P4PP.text:
White recaptures the only way possible.

We will offer a queen trade, relying on our superior pawn structure in an endgame.

r4rk1/p1pp3p/1pn1pqp1/8/2PPQ3/2P2N2/P4PP.text: And we castle, bringing the rook to the semi-open f-file! We have a more compact pawn structure.

r5k1/pbpp2pp/1pn1pq2/8/1bPPP1n1/3B4/PPQ1.text:
But we go to f6, eyeing up the d4-pawn and with the possibility to continue attacking with Qh4.

White is under a lot of pressure. Look at all those pieces stuck on the back rank!

rn1q1k1r/p1p3pp/1p2pn2/6B1/1bPP3Q/2NB4/P.text: Placing pressure on f6. We will exchange a pair of minor pieces to reduce White's attacking potential.

rn1q1k1r/p1p3pp/1p2pn2/6B1/2PP3Q/2PB4/P3.text:
White recaptures with the b-pawn.

We will support our pinned knight with the king, also defending e6 against the coming Nf4 idea.

rn1q1k1r/p1p3pp/1p2pn2/8/1bPP3Q/2NB4/PP2.text:
The queen retreats, pinning our knight.

But now we have time to finally capture the rook.

rn1q1knr/p1p3pp/1p2p3/7Q/1bPP4/2NB4/PP2N.text:
White chooses to develop. White wants to bring the knight to f4, where it will threaten to fork our king and queen.

We develop with gain of time. We do not need to take the rook immediately.

rn1q1knr/p1pp2pp/1p2P3/7Q/1bPP4/2NB4/PP3.text:
Don't take the rook yet! White threatens mate! 

We had better recapture on e6.

rn1q1rk1/pbp3pp/1p1p1n2/3Pp3/2P5/2P2BN1/.text: White castles into safety, and we continue to develop.

rn1q1rk1/pbpp2pp/1p2pn2/3P4/2P5/2P2B2/P3.text:
White develops the knight to e2 since the bishop is already on f3.

We will push forward with e5. We are even threatening to trap their bishop with e4!

rn1q1rk1/pbpp2pp/1p3n2/3Pp3/2P5/2P2BN1/P.text:
White makes room for the bishop to retreat, and guards the e4 square.
 
We will simply strengthen our central point on e5 by playing ...d6.

rn1q3r/p1p2kpp/1p2pn2/6B1/2PP3Q/2PB4/P2K.text:
White opens up an attack on our bishop.

We retreat it back to its natural base on b7.

rn1q3r/pbp2kpp/1p2pn2/6B1/2PP1N1Q/2PB4/P.text:
An attempt from White to attack our kingside.

We will bring out our last undeveloped minor piece.

rn1qk1nr/p1pp2pp/1p2p3/5P1Q/1bPP4/2NB4/P.text: White plays all-out attack! We move the king to the side.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1bPPP3/2NB4/PP.text:
This is the main line, defending e4.

We will strike at the big pawn center with ...f5, remembering that g2 is tender.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/3P1p2/1bP1P3/2NB4.text:
White can play to block the long diagonal.

We will start by capturing on e4, undermining the pawn defense of d5.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/3P4/1bP1B3/2N5/PP.text:
White recaptures.

We continue by developing a piece, attacking the bishop. We could also have considered ...Qh4.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5P2/1bPP4/2NB4/PP.text:
Our bishop was looking at g2, but what if White captures on f5 anyway?

We gobble up the g2-pawn, with the rook to follow!

rn1qk1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5p1Q/1bPPP3/2NB4/.text: Maybe White will give the obvious check. It is not particularly effective. We will just block with the pawn.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5p2/1bPPP3/2NB1P2.text:
f3 defends e4 with the pawn.

Let's take a moment here to reflect our options. We actually have quite a bit of leeway here. Nc6 and Qh4+ are options. Let's go with the latter.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5p2/1bPPP3/2NB4/P.text:
White can choose to defend e4 with the queen.

We will place further pressure on the e-pawn.

White can choose to support e4 via a Qc2/Bd3 battery.

As so often before, we will apply further pressure to the center by developing our knight on f6.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp3p/1p2p1p1/5p2/1bPPP3/2NB4/.text:
White retreats, defending the e-pawn.

We will develop our knight, as before exerting influence on the e4 square.

rn1qk2r/p1pp2pp/1p2pB2/8/1bPPb3/2N5/PP2Q.text:
A valuable intermezzo, removing the defender of our bishop on e4. White needed to do this prior to recapturing on e4, otherwise they would come out of the sequence material down.

We will recapture on f6.

rn1qk2r/p1pp3p/1p2pBp1/8/1bPPb3/2N5/PP2Q.text:
White needs to insert this capture before taking on e4 with the queen.

We recapture on f6.

rn1qk2r/pbpp2pp/1p2pB2/8/1bPP4/2Np4/PPQ2.text: We have this unpleasant intermezzo! We take the d3-bishop, attacking White's queen.  Keep in mind that our light-squared bishop is now also aiming at g2.

rn1qk2r/pbpp2pp/1p2pB2/8/1bPPp3/2NB4/PPQ.text: White should accept that they've simply lost a pawn, but if they try Bxf6 attacking our queen (which worked in previous variations)...

rn1qk2r/pbpp2pp/1p2pn2/3P4/1bP5/2N2B2/PP.text:
White retreats.

We will take on c3, damaging the pawn structure.

rn1qk2r/pbpp2pp/1p2pn2/3P4/2P5/2P2B2/P4P.text: White recaptures, and we will castle.

rn1qk2r/pbpp2pp/1p2pn2/5p2/1bPPP3/2NB1P2.text:
f3 serves to protect e4 and block the diagonal to g2.

We'll develop the other knight, attacking d4.

rn1qk2r/pbpp2pp/1p2pn2/5pB1/1bPPP3/2NB4/.text: Pinning the knight to avoid neutralize some of our pressure. We will initiate exchanges on e4.

This move, played with the idea of pinning our knight, actually loses material.

We simply take on e4 with the pawn.

rn1qk2r/pbpp3p/1p2pnp1/5pB1/1bPPP3/2NB4/.text:
White pins our knight to our queen.

We will initiate exchanges on e4.

rn1qk2r/pbpp3p/1p2pnp1/6B1/1bPPB3/2N5/PP.text:
White recaptures, as we were threatening the bishop.

We will capture on e4 with the bishop.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/2PPP3/2N5/PP3P.text:
White gains space by putting another pawn in the center! An impressive center that we'll have fun undermining.

We began the attack on the center with Bb4, pinning the c3-knight.

rn1qkbnr/pbpppppp/1p6/8/2PP4/2N5/PP2PPPP.text:
White develops the knight to c3, which controls d5 and e4.

We will counter on the light squares by controlling d5 at the very least, and open up our dark-squared bishop's route to b4.

rn2k1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5P1q/1bPP4/2NB1PP1.text:
A natural capture. White has enough pieces protecting f3, and they might see this trade as beneficial.

We will playing in gambit style and develop!

rn2k1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5p2/1bPPP2q/2NB1PP.text: White plays g3, attacking our queen. We will retreat her to h5, eyeing the f3-pawn.

rn2k2r/p1pp2pp/1p2pq2/8/1bPPQ3/2N5/PP3PP.text:
The queen takes back the bishop, attacking our rook.

We will ignore it, and castle! If White takes on a8, we will capture on f2 and White's position will collapse.

rn2k2r/p1pp3p/1p2pqp1/8/1bPPQ3/2N5/PP3PP.text: White takes the bishop, hitting our a8-rook. We will block with the knight.

rn2k2r/pbpp2pp/1p2pn2/5P1q/1bPP1B2/2NB1P.text:
White decides not to fall further behind in development, and brings out a piece with Bf4.

We will castle, placing our rook on an active file in the process.

rn3rk1/p1pp2pp/1p2pq2/8/1bPPQ3/2N2N2/PP3.text: White blocks the attack on f2. We now have to solve the problem of our attacked rook, and we do this by blocking the line of fire with the knight.

rn3rk1/pbp3pp/1p2pn2/7q/1bPP1B2/2NB1PP1/.text: We just recapture. We have better development! We have five active pieces, while White only has three, and the white king is still in the center.

rn3rk1/pbpp2pp/1p2Pn2/7q/1bPP1B2/2NB1PP1.text: Should White persist with pawn grabs...

rnbqkbnr/p1pppppp/1p6/8/2PP4/8/PP2PPPP/R.text:
This move brings another pawn to a location controlling central squares.

We will fianchetto.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/3P4/8/PPP1PPPP/RNB.text:
Now that you've been introduced to positions after White opens with 1.d4, let's analyze what happens after 1.d4 b6 2.c4 Bb7 3.Nc3 e6 4.e4 Bb4 5.Bd3 f5. 

There are many moves that can result, and some of these lines are tricky. Learn them, and you learn the system!

We'll start with 1...b6.

r2qk1nr/1bpn1ppp/1p1p4/p2Pp3/2P1P3/3B1N2.text:
We can play a5, placing another pawn on a dark-square, and securing an outpost for our knight on c5 in the future.

Note that our bishop is better than the white counterpart, due to the pawn configuration.

r2qk1nr/pbpn1ppp/1p1p4/3Pp3/2P1P3/3B1N2/.text: White can opt to close down the center.

r2qk1nr/pbpn1ppp/1p1pp3/8/2PPP3/3B1N2/PP.text:
White gets to safety.

We will break with e5.

rn1q1rk1/pbp1bppp/1p1ppn2/8/2PPP3/2NB1NP.text: But we can castle immediately! From here on, we'll have the possibility of developing our other knight to d7, then playing e5 for counterplay. We have no problems as we emerge from the opening.

rn1qk1nr/pbp1bppp/1p1pp3/8/2PPP3/2NB1N2/.text:
White develops a kingside piece supporting d4.

We will develop our knight, preparing to castle.

rn1qk1nr/pbp2ppp/1p1pp3/8/2PPP3/3B1N2/PP.text:
White chooses to develop, supporting the d4-pawn.

We develop our knight, supporting a future e5 pawn break.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1bPPP3/2NB4/PP.text: Voluntarily stepping into a pin. This is White's most popular response.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1bPPP3/3B4/PP1.text:
Bd2 is a very logical move, blocking the check and attacking the bishop.

We will exchange bishops.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1bPPP3/3B4/PP3.text:
Kf1 is a bit odd, and not super intuitive at the lower levels. Nevertheless, it's the top engine move.

We will simply retreat the bishop to e7. We have spent two moves with our bishop, but ultimately White cannot regain castling rights.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/2PPP3/3B4/PP1N.text:
White recaptures with the knight to develop another minor piece.

In this position Jobava and Mamedyarov have both played 6...d6. We shall do likewise!

This allows us to control some central dark squares after trading the dark-squared bishops.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5p2/1bPPP3/2NB4/P.text:
This allows us to play f5, attacking e4 and our bishop is pressurizing  the long diagonal to g2!

This is known territory, as we have examined this position in the previous study.

rn1qk1nr/pbppbppp/1p2p3/8/2PPP3/2NB4/PP3.text:
White continues with piece development.

Meanwhile we prepare e5 with d6.

rn1qk2r/pbp1bppp/1p1ppn2/8/2PPP3/2NB1NP1.text: White's idea is to castle by hand.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/2PPP3/3B4/PP3P.text:
Now White grabs more central space by pushing a third pawn.

We can proceed by giving a check. As you'll see, White will have to block with a piece or lose castling rights!

rn1qkbnr/pbpppppp/1p6/8/3PP3/3B4/PPP2PPP.text:
White defends the e4-pawn with the bishop.

We play e6, staking a claim to the center and opening up our other bishop.

rnbqkbnr/p1pppppp/1p6/8/3PP3/8/PPP2PPP/R.text:
White adds another pawn to the center!

We fianchetto, attacking e4.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/3P4/8/PPP1PPPP/RNB.text:
Welcome to the final study of this chapter! We'll be looking at how to counter White if they choose to place three pawns in the center and a bishop on d3 supporting e4.

We'll start with 1...b6.

r1q2rk1/p4ppp/1p1p1n2/n1pPp3/Q1P1P3/2P3P.text:
We can use the recently created battery to propose a bishop trade and get to h3 with our queen!

White's pieces on the queenside are very inactive at the moment.

r1q2rk1/p4ppp/1p1p1n2/n1pPp3/Q1P1b3/2P3P.text:
White goes d5, blocking the center.

We can go to f5, creating a bishop and queen battery.

r1q2rk1/p4ppp/1p1p1n2/n1pPpb2/Q1P1P3/2P3.text: If White finally achieves that long-prepared e4 push...

r1q2rk1/p4ppp/1p1ppn2/n1p5/Q1PPb3/2P3P1/.text:
White retreats to defend c4.

But now we can attack with e5!

r1q2rk1/p4ppp/1pnppn2/2p5/Q1PPb3/2P2NP1/.text:
The pawn position is quite closed. There isn't a great location for White to develop their dark-squared bishop to, but let's say they try b2.

We'll play Na5, applying pressure on c4. This is a static weakness for White, and we can play against it.

r2q1rk1/pbpn2pp/1p1pp3/5p2/2PP4/2RBP3/PP.text: And we develop our final minor piece with ideas of returning to f6 (controlling e4), or pushing e5.

rn1q1rk1/pbp3pp/1p1pp3/5p2/2PP4/2RBP3/PP.text: White recaptures with the rook so as to not damage the pawn structure.

rn1q1rk1/pbp3pp/1p1pp3/5p2/2PPn3/2BBP3/P.text:
In positions like this, when one side (in this case Black) has a strong piece in the center, the other side attempts to attack it, to remove it from its strong position.

Taking the dark-squared bishop is preferable over taking a misplaced knight on d2.

rn1q1rk1/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5p2/2PPn3/2BBPN2/.text:
After Rc1 to recapture with a piece and not damage the pawns...

We can continue with a calm d6, a useful pawn move to gain control over some dark squares. Remember: we no longer have a dark-squared bishop.

rn1q1rk1/pbpp2pp/1p2pn2/5p2/1bPP4/2NBPN2.text:
White develops their final minor piece, and the bishop is defending c3. 

We will capture anyway. Our play is all about trying to gain control over e4.

rn1q1rk1/pbpp2pp/1p2pn2/5p2/2PP4/2BBPN2/.text:
White maintains the integrity of their pawn structure.

We will jump our knight into e4.

rn1qk1nr/1bpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/p1PP4/P1Q2N2/1.text:
The queen recaptures to preserve the integrity of the pawn structure.

We will develop our g8-knight, controlling some central squares.

rn1qk1nr/1bpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/pQPP4/P1N2N2/1.text: White could grab our bishop. It looks like a free piece, but we attack the queen with the knight, and it is very short of squares.

rn1qk1nr/1bpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/pbPP4/P1N2N2/1.text:
White retreats to c2, keeping an eye on the knight.

We'll exchange on c3.

rn1qk1nr/1bpp1ppp/1p2p3/p7/1bPP4/PQN2N2/.text: "Ok, that's enough!" says White. Our bishop is attacked with a3. But here we have the very clever reply of ...a4.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1bPP4/1QN2N2/P.text:
Qb3 seems logical, attacking our bishop and defending the c3 knight.

We will support the bishop with the a-pawn, and gain a little space on the queenside.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1bPP4/2N1PN2/P.text:
e3 is also a sound setup, defending the knight on f3 with the queen and deciding that White is not going to worry about Black capturing on c3.

We can play f5! We have a strong grip on the light squares.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1bPP4/2N2NP1/P.text:
Finally, g3 recognizes the value of the diagonal that Black occupied. White wants to fianchetto to counter Black's control of the diagonal.

Here we can proceed to damage the pawn structure.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/2PP4/2P2NP1/P3.text:
White recaptures the only way possible.

We develop with an eye towards e4.

rn1qk1nr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5p2/1bPP4/2NBPN2/.text:
White develops a piece and tries to counter our control of e4.

We will continue our development with ...Nf6, and exert further control over the e4 square.

rn1qk2r/1bpp1p2/1p2p2p/6p1/p1PPn3/P4NB1/.text: White retreats, keeping an eye on our knight on e4.

rn1qk2r/1bpp1p2/1p2pn1p/6p1/p1PP4/P1Q2NB.text:
White retreats the bishop. 

We can jump into the center with a tempo on the queen. Let's do it!

rn1qk2r/1bpp1pp1/1p2pn1p/8/p1PP3B/P1Q2N2.text: White retreats the attacked bishop, but now we will push our g-pawn and decisively break the pin.

rn1qk2r/1bpp1ppp/1p2pn2/6B1/p1PP4/P1Q2N2.text:
White pins our knight to the queen.

We will aim to break the pin with our kingside pawns.

rn1qk2r/1bpp4/1p2p2p/5pp1/p1PPn3/P4NB1/1.text:
We can play f5, supporting our knight on e4!

We'll develop the rest of our pieces, and push in the center with ...d6 and ...e5. We have taken control over a lot of space.

rn1qk2r/pbp2ppp/1p1ppn2/8/2PP4/2P2NP1/P3.text:
White castles into safety.

We will defend our bishop and support a c7-c5 push.

rn1qk2r/pbpp1ppp/1p2pn2/8/2PP4/2P2NP1/P3.text:
White places their bishop on the long diagonal.

Let's place a pawn on a dark square, controlling e5 and remembering that we have traded off our dark-squared bishop.

rn1qk2r/pbpp2pp/1p2pn2/5p2/1bPP4/2NBPN2/.text:
White castles.

We will do likewise.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/2PP4/2N2N2/PP2.text:
And White plays Nf3, supporting d4 and controlling e5.

We bring the bishop out and pin the knight, as we are used to doing. White has three options which we will explore.

rn1qkbnr/pbpppppp/1p6/8/2PP4/2N5/PP2PPPP.text:
White develops a knight, supporting central squares.

We play ...e6, staking a claim to the center, and preparing to activate the f8-bishop.

rnbqkbnr/p1pppppp/1p6/8/2PP4/8/PP2PPPP/R.text:
Controlling the center through a flank pawn.

We will fianchetto our bishop.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/3P4/8/PPP1PPPP/RNB.text:
Congratulations on getting this far! You're practically halfway through. 

In this first study, you'll learn to counter White when they set up with d4/c4/Nc3/Nf3.

In order to remember these variations, you can think of them as Two Knights with d4/c4.

We will prepare to fianchetto.

rnq1k2r/pbp2ppp/1p1ppn2/8/2PP4/2P2NP1/P3.text:
White gets ready to support a pawn push of their own.

We will castle.

rnq2rk1/p1p2ppp/1p1ppn2/8/Q1PPb3/2P2NP1/.text:
Getting the queen out of danger.

We will play c5, as we planned when we played Qc8! Also, we act to place pawns on dark squares, recognizing that we don't have a dark-squared bishop.

rnq2rk1/p4ppp/1p1ppn2/2p5/Q1PPb3/2P2NP1/.text:
White removes the bishop from the diagonal in order to give it scope towards c4 (which is weakly defended). 

We will complete the development of our minor pieces.

rnq2rk1/pbp2ppp/1p1ppn2/8/2PP4/2P2NP1/P1.text:
White plays Qc2. In an ideal world, this would support an e4 pawn push, gaining a big center.

We will act first, cutting across these plans, and place our bishop on e4, attacking the white queen.

r2q1rk1/pb1p2pp/npPbpn2/5p2/1PP5/P1N2NP1.text:
White can choose to capture, in which case we will take back with the pawn.

We can't capture with the bishop, because that would walk into a b5 pawn fork.

r2q1rk1/pbp1b1pp/1p1pp3/5p2/2PPnB2/P1Q1P.text:
We make great use of the e4 square with a tempo. 

From here, we have ideas of piece activation, like Qe8 for Qg6 and also Rd8.

r2q1rk1/pbp1b1pp/1p1ppn2/5p2/2PP1B2/P1Q1.text: With the idea that when White recaptures...

r2q1rk1/pbp1b1pp/1p1ppn2/5p2/2PPnB2/PQN1.text: If the queen comes out to b3,  we initiate a trade on c3...

r2q1rk1/pbpnb1pp/1p1pp3/5p2/2PPnB2/P1N1P.text:
White gets their king to safety...

And we will support our knight on e4.

r2q1rk1/pbpp2pp/1p1bpn2/2nP1p2/2PN4/P1N3.text: White wants to bring their knight into the center, too. White is posing questions to our e6-pawn.

r2q1rk1/pbpp2pp/1p2pn2/2nPbp2/2PN4/P1N3P.text:
We jump into the center, applying pressure to the knight on d4. We are threatening Bxb3 and Nb3!

We generally want to play ...d6 (If White moves the d4-knight) and ...Qe7 to finish development. 

As f4 might inconvenience our bishop, we should also capture the knight on c3 if possible. This will disrupt White's pawn structure, and then we can establish a strong knight on c5.

r2q1rk1/pbpp2pp/np1bpn2/3P1p2/1PP5/P1N2N.text:
White fianchettoes their bishop.

We will continue by undermining the center!

r2q1rk1/pbpp2pp/np1bpn2/3P1p2/2P5/P1N2NP.text: White likewise castles, and our knight hops into c5.

r2q1rk1/pbppb1pp/1pn1p3/5p2/2PP1B2/P1P1P.text:
And we develop our final minor piece.

We can improve the minor pieces by placing the knight on a5 and the dark-squared bishop on f6.

r2qk2r/pbpp2pp/np1bpn2/3P1p2/1PP5/P1N2NP.text: White may seek to fianchetto their light-squared bishop. We will castle.

r2qk2r/pbpp2pp/np1bpn2/3P1p2/2P5/P1N2NP1.text:
White develops another piece.

In response we will castle and get to safety.

r2qkb1r/pbpp2pp/np2pn2/3P1p2/1PP5/P1N2N2.text:
White could choose to expand on the queenside, covering the c5 square.

We can develop our king's bishop on d6, where it controls both sides of the board.

r4rk1/pb2q1pp/nppbpn2/5p2/1PP5/P1N2NP1/4.text: And we connect rooks, finishing our development. We can contemplate central expansion with ...e5, and bringing our queen's rook to the open d-file.

rn1q1rk1/pbp1b1pp/1p1pp3/5p2/2PPnB2/P1N1.text:
White develops their bishop. They intend to castle.

Part of our idea here is to get the knight to f6 to support the e4 knight.

rn1q1rk1/pbppb1pp/1p2p3/5p2/2PP4/P1P2NP1.text:
And so do we.

We'll develop the knight next, and the dark-squared bishop will sit nicely on f6, controlling the diagonal if White decides to push d5.

You'll see we still have to develop our knight on b8. This can be done via a6-c5, should White push forward with d5. If White doesn't push d5, we'll simply jump to c6.

rn1q1rk1/pbppb1pp/1p2p3/5p2/2PPnB2/P1N1P.text:
If white goes for the very natural h3...

we will simply exchange on c3 and double White's pawns.

White defends the threat.

We will place our pawn on d6 to blunt the bishop on f4. This also prepares to develop the knight!

rn1q1rk1/pbppb1pp/1p2pn2/5p2/2PP1B2/P1N1.text:
Play can continue with the very natural h3, giving the bishop a retreat square.

Now we can jump to the center, with a positional threat: taking on c3 to damage the pawn structure.

Developing the bishop and preparing castling.  
 
We will continue with one of our main ideas, and occupy the central e4 square.

rn1qk2r/pbpp2pp/1p1bpn2/3P1p2/2P5/P1N3P1.text:
The bishop gets on the coveted diagonal, supporting the strongpoint on d5.

We will prepare to jump to c5, from where the knight will eye the important e4 square.

rn1qk2r/pbppB1pp/1p2p3/8/2PPp3/P3PN2/1P3.text: White takes our bishop, as their bishop on g5 was attacked twice. Our queen will recapture.

rn1qk2r/pbppb1pp/1p2p3/5pB1/2PPN3/P3PN2/.text: White exchanges off the dominating knight, and we will recapture with the pawn, gaining space and attacking the knight.

rn1qk2r/pbppb1pp/1p2pn2/5p2/2PP1B2/P1N1P.text:
White supports d4 with e3.

We will castle into safety.

rn1qk2r/pbppb1pp/1p2pn2/5pB1/2PP4/P1N1PN.text:
White supports d4.

But now we can make use of that e4 square we control so well.

rn1qkb1r/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5p2/2PP4/P1P2NP1/.text: White recaptures the only way possible, and we will develop our dark-squared bishop.

rn1qkb1r/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5p2/2PPn3/P1N2NP1.text:
White achieves their desired setup.

However, we will now damage the pawns! Our control of e4 yielded us the secondary prize of better pawn structure.

rn1qkb1r/pbpp2pp/1p2pn2/3P1p2/2P5/P1N2N2.text:
White can choose to gain space with this move!

We will bring out our queen's knight, aiming at the c5 square, which is no longer controlled by the white d-pawn.

rn1qkb1r/pbpp2pp/1p2pn2/3P1p2/2P5/P1N3P1.text:
White seeks to deploy their bishop on the h1-a8 diagonal, probably because our bishop is so good on it.

Here we will develop our dark-squared bishop flexibly, exerting pressure on both sides of the white position.

rn1qkb1r/pbpp2pp/1p2pn2/5p2/2PP1B2/P1N2N.text:
Nf3 achieves the same for white: development and central control.

We will develop our bishop and prepare to castle.

rn1qkb1r/pbpp2pp/1p2pn2/5p2/2PP4/P1N2NP1.text:
g3 prepares White's fianchetto. White wishes to contest the good h1-a8 diagonal.

We will make use of the well-controlled e4 square!

rn1qkb1r/pbpp2pp/1p2pn2/5pB1/2PP4/P1N2N2.text:
Maybe White chooses to pin us!

We will break the pin.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/2PP4/P1N5/1P2P.text:
White prevents Bb4 by preemptively playing a3! 

We will  just continue gaining control of e4. Here you'll be introduced to potential responses White might play.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/3P1p2/2P5/P1N5/1P.text:
d5 blocks the diagonal of the b7-bishop and gains space in the center.

We can develop with Nf6, applying pressure on d5 and controlling e4.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5p2/2PP1B2/P1N5/1.text:
Bf4 is also possible should White choose to develop another piece.

We will continue by developing our kingside, controlling key squares.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp2pp/1p2p3/5p2/2PP4/P1N2N2/1.text:
With Nf3 White continues normally, with development and central control.

We will jump to f6, controlling e4 and d5 secondarily. After this White has four main options.

rn1qkbnr/pbpppppp/1p6/8/2PP4/2N5/PP2PPPP.text:
White's knight comes out, supporting central squares.

With ...e6, we prepare to develop our dark-squared bishop. However...

rn2k2r/pbppq1pp/1p2p3/8/2PPp3/P3P3/1P1N1.text:
White retreats, applying pressure on e4.

We will castle, with our rook taking aim at f2!

rn3rk1/pbp1q1pp/1p2p3/3p4/2PPp3/P3P3/1P1.text:
Here we can break in the center, supporting our advanced e4 pawn, while giving our knight a better square to develop to on d7! 

The half-open f-file gives us the chance of a rook lift in the future, with kingside attacking chances!

rn3rk1/pbppq1pp/1p2p3/8/2PPp3/P3P3/1P1NB.text: White needs to castle quickly, so Be2 is necessary!

rnbqkbnr/p1pppppp/1p6/8/2PP4/8/PP2PPPP/R.text:
White plays c4, controlling d5 from the side.

We will develop with ...Bb7 and gain control of the long diagonal.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/3P4/8/PPP1PPPP/RNB.text:
Welcome to the final study of this chapter! You're becoming quite the e6/b6 expert, aren't you? Well in this chapter we'll continue analyzing what happens after white opens with d4 and c4, but what if they prevent our idea of Bb4 pinning the knight with 4. a3? Here you'll find how to respond!

Let's first start with our fianchetto.

4rrk1/pbpp1qb1/np2p1pp/3PPp2/2P5/2N2NP1/.text: White connects rooks, but in the resulting position we have ideas of knight to c5 and then to e4, where we have good control.

r1k1r3/pbpn2bp/1p3np1/1N2pp2/2P2B2/5NP1/.text:
But we're in time to block off the attacker.

We'll continue by attacking the knight on b5 and improving our knight via c5.

r1q2rk1/pbpp2bp/np2pnp1/3P1p2/2P2B2/2N2N.text:
And we move the queen to the side where it defends our bishop and lends some support to our pawn chain.

Play may continue with ideas of Re8, going for an e5 push when it is sufficiently prepared, or by integrating the knight through c5 and e4.

r2q1rk1/p1pP2bp/1p3np1/2n2p2/2PN4/2N3P1/.text: Should White choose to grab a pawn...

r2q1rk1/p1pp2bp/np2Pnp1/5p2/2PN4/2N3P1/P.text:
The king recaptures.

Now we go to c5, applying pressure to the e6-pawn.

r2q1rk1/pbpp2b1/np2pBpp/3P1p2/2P1P3/2N2N.text:
White trades.

And we recapture with a view towards excellent control of the h8-a1 diagonal.

r2q1rk1/pbpp2bp/1p2p1p1/2nP1p2/2P1nB2/P1.text: We can play our f-knight to e4, making use of that central square and proposing a trade of knights. With less space on the board, achieving trades is a good thing.

r2q1rk1/pbpp2bp/1p2pnp1/2nP1p2/2P2B2/P1N.text: After the rook joins a more active file.

r2q1rk1/pbpp2bp/np2Pnp1/5p2/2PN4/2N3P1/P.text:
White opens up the bishop and takes a pawn.

First we will capture that bishop.

r2q1rk1/pbpp2bp/np2pnp1/3P1p2/2P2B2/2N2N.text: White puts their rook somewhere more useful.

r2q1rk1/pbpp2bp/np2pnp1/3P1p2/2P2B2/P1N2.text:
White develops yet another piece, this time applying pressure on c7.

But we can opt for using the recently available c5 square.

r2q1rk1/pbpp2bp/np2pnp1/3P1pB1/2P1P3/2N2.text:
